<description>
The existing BIP352 tests leave several cases insufficiently covered. To identify these gaps, I ran manual mutation testing against `src/common/bip352.cpp`, complemented by `bcore-mutation`. Out of 55 mutations, 33 survived with the existing tests.

With these tests, 52 of the 55 mutations are detected. The three remaining mutations are equivalent to the original implementation.

One mutation replaces the `return std::nullopt` with `break` when `GetOp` fails while scanning a P2PKH scriptSig. The function reaches the same `return std::nullopt` after the loop. Another removes the early return for the case where there are no eligible keys, checking only whether there are no inputs. With no keys, libsecp256k1 already returns a failure, so the result remains `NOT_ELIGIBLE`. The third mutation changes the P2PKH scriptSig scanning loop condition from `pc < txin.scriptSig.end()` to `pc <= txin.scriptSig.end()`. When `pc` reaches the end of the scriptSig, `GetOp` fails, and the function returns the same `std::nullopt`.

The new tests cover scan label reporting, P2PKH public key extraction when the `scriptSig` contains unrelated pushes, invalid public keys across supported input types, P2SH-P2WPKH eligibility, Taproot script-path spends, annex handling, control block validation, prevouts summary errors, Silent Payments destination validation, label copy assignment, maximum-size control block acceptance, and the behavior of `Scan` when none of the outputs is a valid x-only key.

The existing `bip352_skips_transactions_spending_unknown_segwit_versions` test is also extended to cover SegWit versions v2 through v16 and check the exact `NOT_ELIGIBLE` error. The address decoding tests also cover a v0 address with a valid Bech32m checksum but one extra data byte (67 instead of 66). The existing `bip352_scan_skips_invalid_taproot_outputs` test is extended to verify that `Scan` returns an empty list, rather than an error, when none of the outputs is a valid x-only key.

The changes are limited to `src/test/bip352_tests.cpp`. No production code is modified.

The tests also pass on top of the P2SH changes from #36776. The annex-related mutations are detected independently of #36992.

Using `bcore-mutation` with `--one-mutant` and the `bip352_tests` test suite, the mutation score improves from 83.93% (9 of 56 mutations surviving on master) to 91.07% (5 of 56 surviving with the first PR version) and finally to 98.21% (1 of 56 surviving with this version). The only remaining survivor is the equivalent P2PKH loop-boundary mutation described above.

`src/common/bip352.cpp` is not included in the continuous mutation-testing runs on corecheck, so these gaps are not covered by those runs.
</description>
